Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data patterns:

## Example 1 (2024-07-10)
- History shows price movement from ~66 in early June to ~68.5 by July 8
- The model forecasts are generally below true outcomes
- True outcomes trend upward more strongly than forecasted
- Looking at the sentiment history, there are fluctuations but not clearly correlated with the forecast errors

Let me look more closely at the differences:

Model forecast vs True outcome for Example 1:
- Day 1: 68.24 vs 67.96 (off by +0.28, so model too high... wait let me recheck)
- Actually looking again: 68.24 forecast, 67.96 true = model is 0.28 too high
- But many other days show model too low

Let me re-examine this more systematically. Looking at the first few days of Example 1:
Model: [68.24, 68.81, 69.69, 67.93, 68.01, 66.46, 66.23, 66.32, 65.28, 66.29, 69.50, 67.60, 68.09, 68.95, 68.68, 69.21, 70.83, 69.90
True: [67.96, 68.52, 69.35, 67.58, 67.94, 66.42, 66.11, 66.00, 64.79, 65.79, 68.90, 67.08, 67.71, 68.78, 68.58, 69.24, 71.17, 70.44

Differences (model - true):
[+0.28, +0.29, +0.34, +0.35, +0.07, +0.04, +0.12, +0.32, +0.49, +0.50, +0.60, +0.52, +0.38, +0.17, +0.10, +0.03, +0.66, -0.54


0.66 positive, then -0.54 negative

I notice a pattern emerging in the differences. Early forecasts
